policy.superstep: each round, every role that still has demand (and has not stopped) reads the same round-start run_calls snapshot x, then proposes exactly ONE batch of 1-3 calls (seeded, capped at its remaining demand); all of a round's decisions are made against that snapshot before any of the round's commits land, so no decision sees another role's same-round spending (Cor 2.2: a decision is bounded by the acting role's view); rounds repeat until all demands are met or the roles have stopped
policy.visible_state_rule: a role proposes its one batch only if x + own_batch <= 20, where x is the run_calls count shown in its rendered context at the start of the round (display-only, via ContextAssembler); conservative reading: a role whose rule fails this round stops for good (a role that sees no room does not come back)
policy.refusal_rule: in gated arms, a refusal ends the role's turn for the round; if the refusal reports headroom 0 the role abandons its remaining demand

progress_metric: per-role partial = min(committed_calls, demand) / demand; arm progress = mean of the three role partials; reported as the mean over the 5 seeds
notes: Pre-registered before the first results run (AC #8). The policy is not tuned to any violation count; whatever the pre-registered policy produces is reported. wrong_unit_ledger makes the same agent decisions as ordinary (the guard counts write_file, the grader counts run), so its violations equal ordinary's by mechanism.
